blocks.p: Synthetic document for evaluation. Example Widgets Inc. is a fictional company.

Order, inventory and web analytics data live in eleven separate databases. Nightly ETL jobs copy them into a reporting warehouse, but 30% of jobs fail at least once a month, usually from schema drift: a source team renames or retypes a column and the downstream job breaks.
Land raw data in a data lake first, in its original shape, then transform it inside the warehouse (ELT instead of ETL). Transformations become versioned SQL models with tests.

blocks.li: Ingestion: change data capture streams from the three largest databases; daily file drops for the rest.
Storage: an object-storage data lake, partitioned by day.
Transformation: SQL models with schema tests that fail loudly before a bad load reaches dashboards.
Serving: the existing reporting warehouse, unchanged for dashboard users.

blocks.p: Storage and compute add about $14,000 a month; retiring three ETL servers saves $9,000 a month. Migration runs in three phases over nine months, orders first.
Running old and new pipelines in parallel for two months doubles on-call load. Change data capture needs read access to production database logs, which the database team must approve.
